extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, tenants, housing advocates, and other stakeholders preparing comments on HUD proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and submitting public comments on HUD proposed rules, including what content is acceptable, how to locate the rule, submission methods (regulations.gov and Federal Register), and timing/deadline rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / no form letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Form letters will not be considered, so your comments must be original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit templated or copy-paste form letters; tailor your comment to the specific rule and your perspectives or evidence so it is considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and tone flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comment can be long or short, written formally or informally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no required length or style — choose the format that best conveys your points clearly and persuasively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding: research or personal experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be based on research or your own experiences and the experiences of people you know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with research, data, or concrete personal/anecdotal evidence where possible to strengthen the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit via Federal eRulemaking Portal (regulations.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit a comment online through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at www.regulations.gov, where commenters may search for a proposed rule by keywords, agency, document type, and using the rule title or Regulatory Information Number (RIN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regulations.gov to find the correct docket (search by keyword, agency, document type, title, or RIN), fill out the comment form, and upload any supporting files to ensure your comment is recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit via Federal Register website
rubrics_metrics.description: After the rule publishes in the Federal Register, you can search for and view the proposed rule at www.federalregister.gov, and from the rule's page, you can click the green "Submit a Formal Comment" button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clicking the green button opens the formal comment form where you can enter your comment and upload files; use this route if you prefer the Federal Register interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing option exists but electronic submission is recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may also be submitted in writing at the mailing address provided in the proposed rule, but commenters are strongly recommended to submit electronically at www.regulations.gov to ensure receipt before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you mail comments, be aware of postal delays and receipt uncertainty; electronic submission is recommended to guarantee the comment is received and docketed before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and Eastern Time rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All comment deadlines are based on Eastern time, and if the comment deadline is a particular day, you have until 11:59 pm Eastern time that day to complete and submit your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submission timing according to Eastern Time (ET); do not assume local time. Submit well before 11:59 pm ET on the deadline day to avoid last-minute issues.
